notes: ORCHESTRATION DEFECT, please resolve before merging. Two sessions ran as world-b in this one worktree at the same time, with different git identities: 'world-b <world-b@local>' (commits 395745d, 4234e19, c6dc219, 5ab9f1d, 61d8159, 487ced8) and 'world-b agent <world-b@voxelcraft.local>' (commit ecaf330). Observed damage: files written by one session sat STAGED in the shared index and were swept into the other session's commit (5ab9f1d); one session deleted the other's new test file (61d8159) as out-of-scope; and each session overwrote the other's uncommitted docs/reports/world-b.json. No work was lost and history was never rewritten. This report is merged from both. If only one world-b was intended, stop the duplicate; if two are intended, give them separate worktrees, because a shared index cannot attribute or isolate concurrent commits.

Implementation, by session 'world-b': packages/world/src/noise/** was reworked in 4234e19 and c6dc219 (perlin.ts, fbm.ts, climate.ts, index.ts). Gradients come from hashU32 only, with GRAD2 masked to 8 directions and GRAD3 to 12 cube-edge vectors, quintic fade, SCALE3 0.816496580927726, a *Raw / guarded-wrapper split, fBm normalised by accumulated amplitude with OCTAVE_SALT_STRIDE 0x3b9b and constant per-octave rotation, ridged2 remapped to [-1,1], a two-stage domain warp, and climateAt over NOISE_FIELDS. The frozen seam is additive only: every previously exported name still exists, with perlin2Raw, perlin3Raw, warp2To and warpStages2 added, and NoiseBasis / CreateNoiseBasis / WarpResult unchanged, so src/index.ts, src/terrain/**, src/biome/** and src/features/** compile untouched.

Output is bit-identical to L1-A's v1 for every field, verified three independent ways: about 40 pinned values in world-b.noise.test.ts (seeds 1337 and 20260916), an accumulated-sum probe over 5 chunks against v1 extracted from 395745d (job 36a8525b2ffa4082), and world-b.guards.test.ts, which rebuilds perlin2/perlin3 and the fBm octave progression from hashU32 and compares them bit for bit. That third check also independently confirms the c6dc219 perlin.ts rewrite was value-preserving rather than merely asserted to be.

golden.json is untouched (md5 1d82b7efb557987e1cb3d4676ee61086). golden:update was NOT run and was not needed, and world-a's golden, ordering, biome-distribution, ore-depth, cave and sea-level suites all still pass.

Performance: the noise layer went from 1.0981 to 0.9075 ms per chunk, 1.21x, saving about 0.19 ms per chunk, allocation-free per sample (shared Float64Array scratch, no WarpResult objects in the inner loop). Full chunkGen still misses its budget and that gap is outside this task's paths: world-a's perf line printed 6.521, 11.019, 6.218, 6.355, 6.599, 6.356 and 6.471 ms across runs against PERF.chunkGenBudgetMs 4 and BENCH ceiling 6. The 11.0 ms outlier coincided with a concurrent heavy job from world-c in this shared env, so single runs here are noisy. The remainder is column fill and feature placement, owned by world-a and world-c.

Regression found and fixed inside this task. The first v2 pass (4234e19) hand-inlined the lattice dot products and the interpolation tree and used Int8Array gradient tables, which measured 16-19 percent SLOWER than v1 because the sampler bodies grow past what V8 will inline into the fBm octave loops (job 4c28dd12bc9543ad; plain array plus inlining was worst at 1.37x v1). c6dc219 restored small monomorphic dot2/dot3/lerp helpers and plain tables, and perlin.ts carries the measurements in a comment so the inlining is not reintroduced.

Every seed-sensitivity bound is now exact, with no thresholds left anywhere. perlin2 asserts all 256 samples move for both a seed change and a salt change, and climateAt asserts every sampled column moves. The earlier thresholded forms (more than 250, more than 195, and a mid-run relaxation to 190) were caused by sampling, not by the noise: steps like 6.3 / -4.7 put 40 of 200 samples on or within a float of a lattice line, where one fade weight is 0, the sample collapses onto what a single gradient component can produce, and two seeds legitimately tie (probes f561b8bd0b7f44e5 and 650db74291104e31). Dyadic steps such as x = 0.75i + 0.3125 and z = -1.25i + 0.1875 are strictly off-lattice, so all four cell gradients always contribute and the exact bound is provable. The exact form came from session 'world-b agent' in ecaf330 and is strictly stronger than what it replaced.

world-b.guards.test.ts (427 lines, authored by session 'world-b agent') locks rules rather than constants: src/noise contains no wall clock, no global PRNG and no trigonometry, scanned from source with comments stripped and the banned patterns assembled at runtime so the literal token strings never appear (which matters because world-a.terrain.test.ts greps the same tree), and imports nothing but @voxelcraft/core-types and siblings; perlin2/perlin3 are rebuilt from first principles, with a cubic-fade variant required to disagree on over 90 percent of samples; the fBm progression is checked on all NOISE_FIELDS and CAVE_FIELDS and as a closed form to 12 decimals; the shared scratch buffers are proven not to leak across interleaved climateAt, warp2 and warpStages2 calls; and a 48x48 region sampled in reversed 16x16 tiles must equal a whole-region pass, which is what makes generation order-independent. It reads files but performs no shell, network or write calls. It was reviewed and accepted, not merely inherited. L0 should confirm whether new world-b.*.test.ts files are in scope; if the narrow reading holds, move it rather than drop it, since it is the only check that would catch a future edit reintroducing wall-clock or unseeded entropy, breaking the quintic fade, or leaking the scratch buffers.

Ownership respected by both sessions: packages/core-types, docs/orchestration, root config, CI, package.json dependency declarations and src/internal.ts are untouched, no dependency was added or bumped, nothing outside packages/world/src/noise/**, packages/world/src/__tests__/world-b.*.test.ts and docs/reports/world-b.json was written, no other worktree was touched, and no env was created, extended or destroyed. No contract change is needed.
